brief_text:
Package: Reconstruction of 52 rural houses in Kahramanmaraş Province, Afşin District, Turkey under project P180849 using Request for Bids method for civil works.
Status: complete

Timeline: The forecast assumes Invitation for Bids notice type, 28-day advertising period, 7862-character notice length, and English language, but does not account for local contractor capacity or seasonal construction constraints in Turkey. [forecast:5fdadbe55163, benchmark:country_method_category-d495d284]
  model forecast for this package: median 135 days from tender notice to signing (P10 76, P90 289); probability of a slow tender 30% [forecast:5fdadbe55163]
  peer group: median 132 days; 90th percentile 272 days [benchmark:country_method_category-d495d284]
  the forecast median is 3 days longer than the peer-group median

Market approach: Use Request for Bids method as in all 5 close precedents from the same region, with packaging informed by precedent contract amounts ranging from $103,477 to $647,535 and firm participation of 3 to 13 bidders in award notices. [contract:1710851, contract:1710611, contract:1711394, contract:1816777, contract:1813924]

Risks and mitigations:
  1. Payment delays affecting contractors due to postponed commissioning or retained contract guarantees. -> Reinforce coordination within implementing departments to reduce invoice processing times and avoid retaining guarantees until all works are tested. [lesson_chunk:P145529-34182967-0074]
  2. Procurement delays from design finalization issues and late commencement. -> Finalize designs, drawings, and bid documents early before procurement begins. [lesson_chunk:P123828-34118211-0065]
  3. Low competition or re-bidding due to limited local vendor capacity. -> Conduct bidder conferences and training to build capacity among local contractors. [lesson_chunk:P132173-32872360-0069]
  4. Seasonal timing affecting contract implementation when awards occur during rainy season. -> Time contract awards to end of rainy season to allow two full dry seasons for completion. [lesson_chunk:P123828-34118211-0110]

Status: complete

Timeline: The forecast assumes Request for Expression of Interest notice type, 18-day advertising period, 6867-character notice length, and English language, but does not account for project-specific capacity constraints [forecast:3f65f60cd670]. [forecast:3f65f60cd670, benchmark:region_method_category-59d8ada1]

Market approach: Quality And Cost-Based Selection, consistent with 4 of 5 close precedents that used QCBS for BESS consultancy services [contract:1737661, contract:1750071, contract:1754547, contract:1750240], while 1 precedent used Consultant Qualification Selection [contract:1646678]. [contract:1737661, contract:1646678, contract:1750071, contract:1754547, contract:1750240]

Risks and mitigations:
  1. Limited procurement capacity and experience with World Bank procedures may cause processing delays. -> Employ an International Procurement Consultant to assist implementing agencies and transfer knowledge to procurement staff [document_chunk:P152936_24977068_0138]. [document_chunk:P152936_24977068_0138]
  2. Contract management delays and inadequate supervision capacity can result in implementation without proper oversight. -> Ensure strong monitoring from the Borrower and owner engineers with clear contract management arrangements [lesson_chunk:P157055-34286663-0081, lesson_chunk:P133312-34269738-0078]. [lesson_chunk:P157055-34286663-0081, lesson_chunk:P133312-34269738-0078]
  3. Supply chain and logistical issues may cause equipment delivery delays. -> Establish procurement strategy tailored to local context with turnkey contracts placing delivery liability on contractors [document_chunk:P176620_33735225_0082]. [document_chunk:P176620_33735225_0082]
  4. Small contractors may lack financial, technical and E&S capacity leading to non-performance. -> Set technical, E&S and financial criteria for selection during procurement with strong monitoring [lesson_chunk:P157055-34286663-0081]. [lesson_chunk:P157055-34286663-0081]
